Resultantly, a Gram Sabha was convened and resolutions dated 16.08.2022 and 12.09.2022 were passed.
Gram Sabha by passing the resolution had earmarked the land for different projects and works.

However, by order dated 24.01.2023 S.D.O. Lakhnadon, District Seoni directed for construction of certain buildings at the place which were earmarked for Government Primary School, Ganeshganj/Community Centre.

A bare reading of the aforesaid provisions it is clear as day that the principles of natural justice are not applicable before an order of suspension is passed by the competent authority or the same is confirmed by the State Government.
There are two situations under which the prescribed authority can pass an order of suspension relating to an office bearer of Panchayat.

The first condition relates to framing of charges as has been stipulated under section 39(1)(a) of the Act and; the second situation pertains to service of notice along with a charge-sheet to show cause under this Act for his removal from the office.

Sub-section (2) of the aforesaid section confers power on the State Government to confirm the order of suspension passed by the prescribed authority within 90 days from the date of receipt of such report failing which the same is deemed to have been vacated.
Section 40 of the Act deals with removal and that envisages affording an opportunity to show cause and also contemplates due enquiry.
Thus it is apparent that before removal of an office bearer principles of natural justice are to be complied with.

But the said principles are not attracted at the time of passing of the order of suspension by the prescribed authority or later on at the time of order of confirmation passed by the State Government.

As the order of suspension is passed as an interim measure pending removal and there is no express provision natural justice are not applicable,
moreso, when a full fledged enquiry is provided for under section 40 of the Act.

In view of this, the submission of Mr. Tankha that as no opportunity was afforded at the time of passing of suspension order by the prescribed authority the said order is vitiated does not merit consideration.
The same is the position as far as confirmation of the order of suspension is concerned.
But, in the instant case, a meaningful one, the State Government had issued a notice to the petitioner on 26.8.97 requiring him to appear on 15.9.97.
Thus, it is clearly perceptible that the State Government had desired to afford an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner, may be possibly, to satisfy itself.

Though it was not necessary to take recourse to such a procedure but once the State Government thought it appropriate, may be under the prevailing facts and circumstances to hear the petitioner, it is against the concept of propriety to prepone the matter and pass the order of confirmation.
It does not amount to rectification of a mistake.

It may be noted here that the compliance with principles of natural justice cannot be claimed as a matter or right by the petitioner, but once the same has been thought of being afforded and the thought has been concretised by issuance of a notice, hope is kindled in the incumbent to explain his stand to mitigate the situation.

Every authority has to act with propriety, equity and with a sense of doing justice which is apparent as these are the basic tenants which help law and justice to go hand in hand in their conceptual eventuality.

Therefore, the contention of Mrs. Shobha Menon that when there is no mandate in law to hear the petitioner, there Smt. Rajkumari Sayyam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51999321/
5 is no error in passing the order before the date fixed for hearing by the competent authority of the State Government, does not deserve acceptance.

sentences.text: Rule (5) formulated in this decision aptly applies to the present case though it is not a case of a disciplinary action against an employee but against an office bearer of a Panchayat on the ground of his misconduct involving serious consequences.

That rule is as under:--
"(5) Where the enquiry is not governed by any rules/regulations/statutory provisions and the only obligation is to observe the principle of natural justice -- or, for that matter, wherever such principles are held to be implied by the very nature and impact of the order/action -- the Court or the Tribunal should make a distinction between a total violation of natural justice (rule of audi alteram partem) and violation of a facet of the said rule.

In other words, a distinction must be made between "no opportunity"
and no adequate opportunity, i.e. between "no notice" "no hearing" and "no fair hearing"; (a) In the case of former, the order passed would undoubtedly be invalid (one may call it "void" or a nullity if one chooses to).

In such cases, normally liberty will be reserved for the Authority to take proceedings afresh according to law, i.e., in accordance with the said rule (audi alteram partem), (b) But in the latter case, the effect of violation (of a facet of the rule of audi alteram partem) has to be examined from the stand-point of prejudice; in other words, what the Court or Tribunal has to see is whether in the totality of the circumstances, the delinquent officer/employee did or did not have a fair hearing and the orders to be made shall depend upon the answer to the said query".

sentences.text: It is not sufficient to give a mere lip-service to the requirement of law.

It is true that it is not specifically provided in section 40 that principles of natural justice should be 'followed while holding' an enquiry but it is implicit in this provision that the office-bearer who is sought to be removed will be Page: 374 given a fair hearing.

This Court held that the words "after such inquiry as it may deem fit to make" in the main part of section 40(1) of the Act would mean an inquiry which is held in the presence of the office-bearer and not behind bis back.
He should be allowed to inspect the documents which are to be relied upon against him and he should have the right to adduce his own evidence.

sentences.text: It is not the subjective choice of the prescribed authority to get an inquiry held of any kind.
It does not envisage a secret enquiry or a preliminary enquiry alone.
That is made only for collection of evidence and at that stage there is no participation of the person against whom the action is sought to be taken.
The words "as it may deem fit" have to be construed objectively and would mean an inquiry depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
Some of the facts of the inquiry may be excluded if the facts are not very much in dispute or there are other circumstances to dispense with them.
But the office bearer has a right of fair hearing.
"You must hear the person who is going to suffer".
That is a duty which lies upon every one who decides anything.
There is, however, some flexibility depending upon the subject-matter.

Similar is the law laid down by this court in Raja Rai Singh v. State of M.P.,
[2001 (4) MPLJ 364 : 2000 (2) JLJ 242].

sentences.text: Undisputedly, C.E.O. was not a competent authority to remove the petitioner from the post of Sarpanch.
The basic purpose of preliminary fact finding inquiry is to point out as to whether there is some substance in the allegations requiring further proceedings or not?
The purpose of preliminary inquiry is not to hold the person guilty.

Once the competent authority was under impression or was satisfied that there is sufficient material to proceed against the petitioner, then a show cause notice dated 13.06.2023 was issued by C.E.O. Jila Panchayat Seoni requiring the petitioner to appear and to show cause as to why she may not be removed from the post of Sarpanch, Gram Panchayat Ganeshganj in exercise of power under Section 40 of Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam.

sentences.text: After the reply was taken nothing was done by C.E.O. Jila Panchayat, Seoni and order of removal dated 12.09.2023 was passed.

From the removal order dated 12.09.2023 it is clear that C.E.O. Jila Panchayat, Seoni had reproduced the findings given by C.E.O. Janpad Panchayat,
Lakhnadon and thereafter, it was mentioned that a show cause notice was issued to petitioner which was duly replied by her on 21.08.2023.
It is further mentioned that an opportunity of hearing was given on 12.09.2023.

However, petitioner has failed to prove that allegations against her are not correct and thereafter, giving a finding with regard to certain lapses in the auction proceedings as well as non-summoning of monthly meeting, it was held that petitioner is guilty of serious misconduct.
No witness was examined by the department.

16. The impugned order dated 12.09.2023 was basically based on the findings recorded by C.E.O.
Janpad Panchayat, Lakhnadon.
It is made clear that any report submitted by Commission or any preliminary report submitted by fact finding inquiry committee cannot be treated as an evidence.
It is merely an opinion of author of the said inquiry.
The said inquiry report can also not be considered as a judgment because the fact finding committee is not a Court.

Therefore, the findings recorded by the fact finding inquiry committee cannot be relied upon and after the notice under Section 40 of Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam was issued, a detailed inquiry was required in the light of judgments passed by this Court in the cases of Ballabh Das Satal (supra),
Kailash Kumar Parmanad Dangi (supra) and Vikram Singh (supra).

therefore, the same cannot be given the stamp of approval.

17. Accordingly, order dated 12.09.2023 passed by C.E.O.-cum- Prescribed Authority, Jila Panchayat Lakhnadon, District Seoni and order dated 11.10.2023 passed by Commissioner, Jabalpur in File No.2598/Reader/Ji.Pan./2023 and Appeal No.178/Appeal/2023-24 respectively are hereby quashed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
A bare reading of the aforesaid provisions it is clear as day that the principles of natural justice are not applicable before an order of suspension is passed by the competent authority or the same is confirmed by the State Government.
Thus it is apparent that before removal of an office bearer principles of natural justice are to be complied with.
As the order of suspension is passed as an interim measure pending removal and there is no express provision natural justice are not applicable,
moreso, when a full fledged enquiry is provided for under section 40 of the Act.
Though it was not necessary to take recourse to such a procedure but once the State Government thought it appropriate, may be under the prevailing facts and circumstances to hear the petitioner, it is against the concept of propriety to prepone the matter and pass the order of confirmation.
It does not amount to rectification of a mistake.
It may be noted here that the compliance with principles of natural justice cannot be claimed as a matter or right by the petitioner, but once the same has been thought of being afforded and the thought has been concretised by issuance of a notice, hope is kindled in the incumbent to explain his stand to mitigate the situation.
Every authority has to act with propriety, equity and with a sense of doing justice which is apparent as these are the basic tenants which help law and justice to go hand in hand in their conceptual eventuality.
In State Bank of Patiala v. S.K. Sharma, (1996) 3 SCC 364 : AIR 1996 SC 1669 the Supreme Court after exhaustive survey of the earlier precedents has formulated the test of prejudice, that is, whether the person has received a fair hearing considering all things.
But keeping in view the facts of the case certain facets of natural justice as stated above were not complied with resulting in prejudice to the petitioner.
He was not permitted to adduce his own evidence to rebut the material collected against him.
In Ballabhdas v. State of M.P.1998 (2) JLJ 303, it has been observed by this Court that a full fledged enquiry is provided under section 40 of the Act.
This Court in Kailash Kumar Parmanand Dangi v. State of M.P, [1999 (2), MPLJ 722] has held that in such matters the enquiry held behind the back of Sarpanch, cannot be relied upon.
The basic fault in the impugned order is that an inquiry held by the B.D.O, behind the back of the petitioner has been held to be a valid 'inquiry' under section 40 of the Act and he has been packed up on the basis of that inquiry without even supplying a copy of the same to the petitioner, and without affording him an opportunity to lead his own evidence even when he repeatedly asked for the same.
The action of removal and disqualification has to be struck down as there has been a failure of justice.
The guilty must be punished but the finding of guilt has to be arrived after fair hearing which was denied in this case.
As observed in Delhi Transport Corporation v.
DTC Mazdoor Congress, 1991 Supp (1) SCC 600 : AIR 1991 SC 101
It does not envisage a secret enquiry or a preliminary enquiry alone.
That is made only for collection of evidence and at that stage there is no participation of the person against whom the action is sought to be taken.
The words "as it may deem fit" have to be construed objectively and would mean an inquiry depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
Some of the facts of the inquiry may be excluded if the facts are not very much in dispute or there are other circumstances to dispense with them.
Similar is the law laid down by this court in Raja Rai Singh v. State of M.P.,
[2001 (4) MPLJ 364 : 2000 (2) JLJ 242].
10.
The purpose of preliminary inquiry is not to hold the person guilty.
